_about: California, Nov 3 2026: statewide offices and the 14 propositions. Research and sources: docs/launch-content/california-2026-general.md.

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 1: Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs
ballotMeasures.summary:
Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs. Legislative Statute.

$11.25 billion in state general obligation bonds for affordable housing, veterans' mortgages, supportive housing and down-payment help.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/1/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 2: Increases State's Rainy Day Fund
ballotMeasures.summary:
Increases State's Rainy Day Fund. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.

Raises the size of the state's budget reserve used during economic downturns.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/2/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 3: Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes
ballotMeasures.summary:
Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.

Makes permanent the existing higher income-tax rates on earners over about $371,000, which would otherwise expire in 2031.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/3/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 4: Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns
ballotMeasures.summary:
Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns. Legislative Statute.

Lets state and local governments publicly fund candidate campaigns, but not with education, transportation or public-safety funds.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/4/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 5: Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers
ballotMeasures.summary:
Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.

Fills a recalled statewide officer's seat by a later special election or appointment, not by a replacement vote on the same ballot.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/5/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 37: Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes
ballotMeasures.summary:
Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes. Initiative Statute.

$25 billion in bonds to fund fixed-rate loans for up to 17% of the price of new homes under about $1.5 million, repaid by borrowers' mortgage payments rather than the state.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/37/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 38: Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research
ballotMeasures.summary:
Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research. Initiative Statute.

$8.4 billion in bonds for immunology research, half to one UC-affiliated nonprofit institute and half to grants.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/38/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 39: Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification
ballotMeasures.summary:
Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.

Requires government ID to vote in person, and the last four digits of an ID number on mail-ballot envelopes.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/39/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 40: Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers
ballotMeasures.summary:
Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers. Initiative Constitutional Amendment and Statute.

A one-time 5% tax on certain taxpayers with assets over $1 billion, mainly for health care.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/40/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 41: Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes
ballotMeasures.summary:
Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.

Voids state taxes enacted after January 1, 2026 that are exempted from the spending limit, and requires audits of programs funded by new special taxes.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/41/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 42: Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes
ballotMeasures.summary:
Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.

Bans new state taxes on owning non-real-estate property, and retroactive state taxes; voids conflicting taxes enacted after January 1, 2026.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/42/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 43: Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services
ballotMeasures.summary:
Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.

Raises the vote needed to pass citizen-proposed local special taxes from a majority to two-thirds, starting in 2027.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/43/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 44: Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services
ballotMeasures.summary:
Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services. Initiative Statute.

Penalizes nonprofit federally qualified community clinics that spend less than 90% of revenue on program services.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/44/

ballotMeasures.title: 2026 Midterm · California Proposition 45: Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects
ballotMeasures.summary:
Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects. Initiative Statute.

Sets deadlines under CEQA to speed environmental review and lawsuits for many housing, transportation, water and health projects.

Official title; summary from the official Voter Information Guide. Source: https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/45/
